source_reviews.independent_solution: Concept 20 for n=3 gives triangle sum 2d; concept 4 gives triangle sum 180 degrees. Therefore d=90 degrees, consistently making 4d=360 in concepts 24/25. Feasible convex polygon sums are 180*k with integer k>=1. Thus 9180=180*51 gives n=53; 3600=180*20 gives n=22; 2040/180=34/3 gives noninteger n=40/3 and is impossible; 11d=990 gives noninteger n=15/2 and is impossible; 18d=1620=180*9 gives n=11.

source_reviews.task: Actually derive different proofs of both theorems, avoiding a circular exterior-sum argument.
source_reviews.independent_solution: Triangle route 1: draw through A a parallel to BC; the straight half-plane containing B/C splits into the A sector and two sectors equal to B/C by alternate-interior angles, hence total 180. Unlike the actual 491 proof, there are no C-side extensions or vertical-angle substitution. Triangle route 2: half-turn ABC about midpoint AC to send A to C and B to P, and about midpoint BC to send B to C and A to Q. Congruence gives angle PCA=A and angle BCQ=B. P=A+C-B, Q=B+C-A imply P+Q=2C, so CP/CQ are opposite rays. With C as origin, det(A-B,A)=det(A-B,B)=det(A,B) has the same nonzero sign, so CA/CB lie inside one straight half-plane. The three congruent adjacent sectors sum to 180. Polygon route 1: an interior point O joined to all n vertices forms n triangles inside a convex polygon. Their sums total n*180; O's sectors total 360; the remaining sectors exactly exhaust the polygon's interiors, giving (n-2)*180=2d(n-2). Polygon route 2: inductively split off triangle V1V2V3 by diagonal V1V3, leaving a convex (n-1)-gon; additive split angles give S_n=180+S_(n-1)=180*(n-2), starting from the triangle. Neither polygon route invokes theorem 49. The excluded current polygon proof has not been read, so exact nonidentity with it remains UNKNOWN.
